reflux_why: Middling (1.0 per essence). Dream's price is its condition, not its heat: half its casts are wasted if you stand in the wrong place, so it should not also be punished in reflux; but its control is strong enough that it must not be spammable either.
rule: A Dream skill takes hold only of a mind that can see it (you, or the thing you made, inside the target's front arc with a clear line) or that is asleep; it ignores armour and shields, does +30% to the Dazed and the Asleep, and its statuses last half again as long on them. Mindless things - constructs, stone - never feel it.
rule_why: design/14's first pass said 'needs the target to see it or to sleep'. Made exact so it can be built and read: 'sees' is the existing front-arc test (enemy.is_in_front) plus a clear line, so Dream is the reverse of the rear-hit rule - it wants the enemy looking at you. Two things added: the mind has no armour (so a Pavise Bearer, which watches you over its shield, is Dream's best target, where Light and bolts stop on the shield), and constructs, being concepts with nothing to dream with [B: constructs don't want anything], are untouched. Blinded and turned-away enemies are safe from it, which gives Light and Dream a real conflict.

skills.name: Dozing Mote
skills.summary: A slow, drifting mote: 45, and the target nods. The first mote Dazes it; a second on a Dazed target puts it to sleep for 4 s. It must see the mote coming.
skills.verb_fit: Sleep is to put to sleep. Every mote pushes the target one step further down: awake, Dazed, asleep. That is the whole skill.

new_mechanics.name: sees_caster
new_mechanics.definition: Every Dream hit first checks the target: the source (caster, or the conjured thing) must be inside its front arc (is_in_front) with no wall or stone between, and it must not be Blinded - unless it is Asleep. A target that fails takes nothing at all from the hit.

new_mechanics.name: mind_weight
new_mechanics.definition: Dream's control statuses (asleep, terrified, soothed, masked, commanded) last half as long on heavy enemies (shove_resist under 1), and on elites (the Wall Commander) become Dazed instead; constructs and stone take nothing.

new_mechanics.name: asleep
new_mechanics.definition: Asleep (1 stack, 4 s): cannot move or act. Applied to a target that is not already Dazed, it Dazes it instead. Any damage wakes it at once (the waking hit gets Dream's +30% if it is a Dream hit), and waking leaves it Wakeful.

new_mechanics.name: wakeful
new_mechanics.definition: Wakeful (1 stack, 6 s): cannot be put Asleep; a sleep effect Dazes it instead.

good_modifiers.word: A deep sleep: 6 s instead of 4.
A quicker mote, harder to step out of the way of.
A second, dreamt mote leaps on to one more target.
What it does not drop, it calms: the target stops starting attacks for a moment.

bad_modifiers.why: Its own opposite: a sleep bolt that rudely wakes its sleepers. The fallback adds +50% against Asleep targets, which this skill's own hit then wakes and cannot re-sleep (Wakeful).
Terror and sleep fight each other: the fallback makes the target flee instead of nodding, so the second mote never lands.
Shoving a body you are lulling makes no sense; the fallback knocks the target out of your pools and out of reach of the second mote.

skills.name: Rousing Blow
skills.summary: One enemy in reach: a heavy blow. On a sleeper it is a rude waking: double damage and 80 poise, enough to stagger most.
skills.verb_fit: Wake is to rouse, to break a trance. The skill is the cash-in for everything Sleep set up: the blow is the waking, and waking is what hurts.

good_modifiers.word: Wind up over a sleeper - it is not going anywhere - for 30% more.
Everything into one waking: 25% harder.
It wakes on the floor: 30% more poise damage, a sure stagger.
It wakes into a nightmare: Terrified, running, its back to you.

bad_modifiers.why: Its own opposite: the blow that wakes puts it back to sleep - and the target is Wakeful, so the fallback only Dazes it.
One waking spread thin: the strike has one target, so the fallback only takes 15% off the blow.
A soothing blow is a contradiction, and Soothed ends the moment it is hit; the fallback does nothing.

skills.name: Doubling Step
skills.summary: Step 5 m aside and leave a phantom of yourself behind for 3 s. Enemies that were watching you go for the phantom instead; it breaks at the first blow.
skills.verb_fit: Conjure makes an illusion. The step is only there to get you out of the picture; the skill is the conjured double left standing in it.

leave_decoy.fools: enemies that see you as you cast

new_mechanics.name: leave_decoy
new_mechanics.definition: A dash with leave_decoy leaves a phantom of the caster at the start point for life seconds; every enemy that passed sees_caster at the cast targets the phantom instead of the caster (melee walks to it, archers aim at it) until it breaks after breaks_on_hits hits or a Lit/Dispel effect pops it.

good_modifiers.word: A phantom that holds them for 4.5 s.
A 6.5 m step, farther from the trap.
Out of the step a quarter sooner, free to act while they swing at nothing.
They keep believing it 30% longer.

bad_modifiers.why: Its own opposite: breaks the illusion it makes. The dash has no hit for its interrupt, so the fallback does nothing but undo the phantom.
Reveals the disguise you just put up; the dash has no hit to carry Read.
The step touches nobody, so there is no one to pin; the fallback does nothing.

skills.name: Shattered Dream
skills.summary: Every enemy within 10 m under one of your Dream spells wakes from it at once: 50 each, 100 to sleepers, and all of them are Dazed for 2 s. Your phantoms burst for 40.
skills.verb_fit: Dispel breaks illusions. Every spell you have laid on the room is broken at once, and breaking a dream is what does the damage.

good_modifiers.word: Break every dream within 14 m.
A rude waking for the whole room: +50% on sleepers and more poise.
All of it, once: 20% harder.
They wake on the floor: 30% more poise damage.

bad_modifiers.why: Its own opposite: conjuring while breaking illusions. A detonate has no chain, so the fallback's extra jump does nothing.
It wakes them and then tries to put them back - and they are Wakeful, so the fallback only Dazes the already Dazed.
Nothing travels; the fallback has no speed to raise.

skills.name: Night Terror
skills.summary: For a moment you are the thing under the bed: everything within 4 m that sees you takes a blow and is Terrified for 2 s - it turns, runs, and will not attack.
skills.verb_fit: Dread is terror. The blow is small; the point is the fear, and fear only works on those who are looking at you.

new_mechanics.name: terrified
new_mechanics.definition: Terrified (1 stack, 2 s): turns and moves away from the source at walking speed and starts no attacks; its back is to you, so hits on it count as from behind - but it no longer sees you, so Dream cannot reach it until it turns.

good_modifiers.word: A wider terror, 5.2 m: the whole slot ring breaks.
They run for 3 s.
The fear sticks 30% longer.
They fall over themselves: 30% more poise damage.

bad_modifiers.why: Its own opposite: calm and terror cancel. The fallback Soothes them, which ends at once because the burst just hit them.
Pulling in the very enemies you are sending running is a contradiction; the fallback drags them 1.5 m closer as they flee.
Enraging what you are terrifying makes no sense (and frenzy is the enemy's tool); the fallback is just +20% damage for more essence.

skills.name: Quiet Hour
skills.summary: Point, 9 m: a hush 3.5 m across for 7 s. Enemies in it that see it are Soothed: they move 30% slower and start no attacks. Hitting one snaps it out.
skills.verb_fit: Soothe is calm and bliss. The zone harms nothing; it makes a patch of the fight where nobody wants to fight.

new_mechanics.name: soothed
new_mechanics.definition: Soothed (1 stack, while in the zone and 1 s after): moves at 70% and starts no attacks (one already winding up finishes); ends on that enemy the moment it takes a hit.

good_modifiers.word: A hush that lasts 10.5 s.
A wider hush, 4.5 m.
In the quiet the Dazed drop off: Soothed enemies that are Dazed fall Asleep.
The hush settles you as well: 20% less reflux.

bad_modifiers.why: Its own opposite: terror in a zone of calm. The fallback sends everyone in it running, out of the zone.
Enrage and soothe cancel; the zone deals no damage, so the fallback's +20% does nothing.
A shove every tick is a hit that breaks Soothed, so the zone would undo itself.

skills.name: Changeling Mask
skills.summary: One enemy within 10 m that sees you wears your face for 4 s. Its friends within 8 m that see it take it for you and attack it, and it fights back.
skills.verb_fit: Mimic is to take another's look. Here the look taken is yours, laid over an enemy: a disguise worn by the wrong person.

new_mechanics.name: gaze
new_mechanics.definition: An instant Dream effect on one enemy within range (or on the enemy nearest a point, if the skill says so) that passes sees_caster; no travel, no projectile, blocked only by walls and stone.

new_mechanics.name: masked
new_mechanics.definition: Masked (1 stack, 4 s): wears the caster's look; its allies within lure_radius that can see it treat it as the player (target it, claim slots on it, shoot it) and it answers them in kind.

good_modifiers.word: The mask holds for 6 s: a proper brawl.
Mask the one at the back, 14 m away.
Fooling allies up to 10.4 m away.
The likeness sticks 30% longer.

bad_modifiers.why: Its own opposite: revealing the disguise you are laying. The fallback (Read) ends the mask on the same target.
Shoving the masked one away from the allies you want to fight it defeats the skill.
A gaze has no projectile to pierce, and Dream already ignores armour; the fallback does nothing.

skills.name: Read the Tell
skills.summary: One enemy within 12 m that sees you shows its hand for 8 s: every attack it starts can be interrupted, and any hit during its wind-up staggers it. Works on elites.
skills.verb_fit: Unmask reveals a disguise. The disguise here is the enemy's poker face: you see through it to what it is about to do.

new_mechanics.name: read
new_mechanics.definition: Read (1 stack, 8 s): every attack it starts is flagged interruptible (white flash), and a hit that lands during its wind-up staggers it; ends Masked and pops any illusion on it. Not reduced by mind_weight: elites can be Read.

good_modifiers.word: 12 s of its hand on the table: a whole Commander phase.
You keep reading it 30% longer.
Read it from 16.8 m, before it closes.
Read two of them at once.

bad_modifiers.why: Its own opposite: putting a mask on the face you are unmasking; the fallback Masks the target and the two statuses cancel.
A short read (4.8 s) often ends before the attack comes; the gaze has no damage for the +25%.
A gaze has no force; the fallback is a free shove that moves the target out of the reach you want to punish it in.

skills.name: Errand
skills.summary: Point, 10 m: the enemy nearest that spot that can see you (or is asleep) walks to it and stands there 2 s without attacking - into your pool, out of the line, away from the Drummer. A hit breaks it.
skills.verb_fit: Whisper plants a command. The skill is one order, 'go there', and the enemy carries it out as if it were its own idea.

new_mechanics.name: commanded
new_mechanics.definition: Commanded: walks by its path to the chosen point, then stands stand_s; starts no attacks meanwhile; ends at once if hit. Whispered to a sleeper, it does not wake it, and the errand starts when it wakes.

good_modifiers.word: Send it to a spot 14 m away.
It stands there 3 s.
The two nearest walk.
It walks off without calling for help.

bad_modifiers.why: Putting it to sleep (or Dazing it) at the moment of the order means it never walks; the two words fight.
A Terrified enemy runs away from you, not to your spot; the fallback overrides the errand.
A shove is a hit, and a hit breaks the command; the fallback undoes the skill.

skills.name: Shutter
skills.summary: Point, 10 m: minds within 3.5 m that see it close up: 25, and for 8 s they cannot be Drummed or Roused, and cannot call for help or answer a call.
skills.verb_fit: Shut closes the mind to others. Turned on the enemy, it cuts each one off from the drum, the shouted order and the cry for help.

new_mechanics.name: shut
new_mechanics.definition: Shut (1 stack, 8 s): Drummed and Roused end and cannot be applied; it cannot send the reinforcements signal and is not counted when an ally's call is answered; a Drummer that is Shut cannot drum.

good_modifiers.word: Shut a 4.5 m circle: the whole drummed line.
Closed for 12 s.
Drop it on the Drummer 14 m back.
A shut mind drops what it was about to do: it interrupts.

bad_modifiers.why: Its own opposite: planting a command in a mind you are closing; the fallback pulls them toward you.
Nothing travels; the fallback has no speed to raise.
Lifting bodies has nothing to do with the mind; the fallback is a free Updraft.
